rules.title: Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not terminate a tenancy without just cause, and must pay relocation assistance for no-fault evictions. At-fault causes include failure to pay rent, uncured lease violations, nuisance or damage, illegal use, failure to renew a similar agreement, denying reasonable access, and an unapproved subtenant. No-fault causes include owner or family move-in, required resident manager move-in, demolition or removal from the rental market, a government order to vacate, HUD sale, residential hotel conversion, and conversion to affordable housing.
rules.coverage_text: Most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO), including buildings newer than October 1, 1978 and properties with only one single-family dwelling. It applies to a tenancy once the tenant has lived in the unit for at least six months or the original lease has expired, whichever comes first.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate, cooperatives under certain circumstances, some non-profit facilities for the homeless or short-term treatment centers for substance abuse, and some properties owned by HACLA or the government. Tenants evicted for at-fault reasons are not entitled to relocation assistance.
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.interaction_text: The JCO covers most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles that are not regulated by the City’s Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).

rules.title: Evictions for Non-Payment of Rent (Fair Market Rent threshold)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR) for the unit's bedroom size.
rules.key_value: Amount owed must exceed the Fair Market Rent (FMR) for the unit's bedroom size
rules.coverage_text: All RSO and JCO rental units in the City of Los Angeles.
rules.quoted_span: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).

rules.title: Eviction Notices Filed with LAHD
rules.requirement: All eviction notices issued to tenants in the City of Los Angeles must be filed with LAHD within three (3) business days of service on the tenant.
rules.key_value: within three (3) business days of service
rules.coverage_text: All JCO and RSO rental properties in the City of Los Angeles.
rules.quoted_span: Applies to all JCO & RSO rental properties – All eviction notices issued to tenants in the City of Los Angeles must be filed with LAHD within three (3) business days of service on the tenant.

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482) rent cap
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region, or 10%, whichever is lower. The page states the maximum allowable increase was 8.9% from August 1, 2024 to July 31, 2025 and 8.8% from August 1, 2023 to July 31, 2024.
rules.key_value: 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region, or 10%, whichever is lower
rules.coverage_text: Buildings older than 15 years, other than the exempt properties listed.

rules.exemptions: Units constructed within the last 15 years (rolling); units restricted by a deed, regulatory restriction or recorded document limiting affordability to low or moderate-income households; certain dormitories; a two-unit property where the second unit was occupied by an owner for the entire tenancy; single-family homes and condominiums not owned by a real estate trust, corporation, or LLC with at least one corporate member, where the landlord notified the tenant in writing as described in Civil Code Sections 1946.2(e)(8)(B)(i) and 1947.12(d)(5)(B)(i). The single-family exemption does not apply where there is more than one dwelling unit on the lot or a second unit that cannot be sold separately; units already subject to the City's RSO.
